answer.evidence: The cap width profile runs 5, 9, 11, then 13 for rows 4-8. It is rounded only at the upper edge. Rows 7-8 are a teal underside band that stays at full width 13, then row 9 drops to 9 and the shaft is 7 wide. This is a dome or hat with a flat bottom sitting on a narrower shaft. It is not an ellipse plate bounded by narrower rows above and below, and no front-edge line separates a top surface from the face. The shaft and sign panel (rows 10-22) are drawn as flat vertical faces, and the flared base (rows 27-30) is a plain front face with no visible top. The whole object reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style sign post: a rounded white-grey cap, a pale shaft and an orange number plate on a dark base. Measured facts: 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile, equal to kiosk-a (12) and above bus-shelter-a (6), though below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint, as it does in every reference. The shaft shows about 4 lightness steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow side) against about 5 on the references. It is a thin, single-tile object, so the density fact is not used against it. By eye it sits acceptably next to the references and does not look sticker-like, although it is a little simpler than vending-a. It is a close match to the shipped modern_city art.
